newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Waterford Co-op meeting still going on.
newsitem.headline: Waterford Co-op meeting still going on.

text.p: A meeting of Waterford Co-Op, which was due to discuss a 281 million punt bid for Waterford Foods Plc, was still going on at 1530 GMT (1630 local time) on Friday, a spokesman for Waterford Foods said.

But the meeting was unlikely to come to any conclusions about the merger proposal from local rival Avonmore Foods which would create a new group with a combined turnover of 2.5 billion Irish pounds, he said.
To succeed the merger must be ratified by 75 percent of Waterford Co-op members who own 67 percent of the company's shares.
A survey by the Irish Farmers Journal shows opinion on a merger to be evenly split among Waterford shareholders with 51 percent of 126 shareholders surveyed in favour of a merger with another group.
Irish state television said most of the members would not comment on their way into the meeting although a number of them said they hoped the proposal would be rejected.
Waterford Foods' share price was down two pence at 95 Irish pence per share by 1550 GMT.
This is well below the 117.5 pence they would be worth if the takeover was successful and indicates that there are doubts in the market about the prospects of the deal going ahead.
